A Sherpa mountaineer who, with the New Zealander Edmund Hillary, made the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest on 29 May 1953. He lived from 1914 to 1986.

He was born in the Khumbu region of Nepal or, by some accounts, just across the border in Tibet, and grew up among the Sherpa people. As a young man he moved to Darjeeling, where British expeditions hired porters, and he joined Everest attempts from the 1930s on. In 1952 he and the Swiss climber Raymond Lambert came within a few hundred metres of the summit.

The next year he joined the British expedition led by John Hunt. He and Hillary reached the top together, and both long refused to say who stepped up first. Tenzing became a hero in India, Nepal and beyond, honoured by both countries and by Britain. He later led field training at the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute in Darjeeling. His fame made "Sherpa" a word known worldwide and opened the way for Sherpas to become leading climbers in their own right.
sum: A Sherpa mountaineer who, with the New Zealander Edmund Hillary, made the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest on 29 May 1953. He lived from 1914 to 1986.
